body:
**Ruling (operator, 2026-11-12): option (a) — the rail serving an id is not an allowance.**

A rail-served id the catalog does not list stays unlisted and inadmissible: an admission naming one keeps deferring `not-in-catalog` (ruling 4 stands: never a fallback price, and a pay-as-you-go row is not a Go price). The rail's `/zen/go/v1/models` answer stays unread: no third read, no `served` flag, no reference price. This holds for all three classes of the 2026-10-20 investigation (A deprecated-but-served, C1/C2 pay-as-you-go without a Go row, C3 no vendor row).

Checked today against the 2026-11-11 snapshot: none of the eight is a tier loss (`qwen3.8-max` is the listed successor of `qwen3.7-max`; `omen-alpha` still has no models.dev row under any provider).

What closes this issue: GW-CATALOG-GO's `⚑ gap: a rail-served id the catalog does not list` row becomes the ruled behaviour, and the dated `⚑ gap (2026-10-20, PR #2766 → work #2768)` clause in the index row is trimmed. The sibling `⚑ gap: listed is not alive` stays standing, with the shadow cells and the 4xx/5xx belts as the liveness signal. The seat carries the spec PR.
